jurisdictions.name: Providence
jurisdictions.office: City of Providence Department of Inspection and Standards
notes: Providence publishes a Rhode Island Pool Barrier Checklist and says a permit is required for a pool or spa that can hold 24 inches or more of water.

The checklist (October 21, 2025) says it incorporates the 2018 edition of the International Swimming Pool and Spa Code, while the state code adopts the 2021 edition, so the edition should be confirmed with the city.
It lists a barrier at least 48 inches tall, no openings that pass a 4 inch sphere, a 36 inch clear zone around pumps and filters, and self-closing, self-latching gates that open away from the pool.
Under the zoning section it cites, no private pool or hot tub, including aprons and walks, may be in a front yard or a required corner or interior side setback.
The pool and its impervious apron count toward the rear yard and total impervious maximums.

sources.title: Rhode Island Pool Barrier Checklist (City of Providence), 10.21.25
Brochures, Applications and FAQ (City of Providence Inspection & Standards)

jurisdictions.name: Cranston
jurisdictions.office: Cranston Department of Building Inspections & Zoning
notes: The city's Building Inspection page says its department enforces the current edition of the Rhode Island State Building Code, the International Codes and the National Electrical Code as amended.
It says any contractor working on another person's home must be licensed or registered by the State of Rhode Island.
The department moved to 155 Gansett Avenue (rear) on March 23, 2026.

jurisdictions.name: Barrington
notes: Private residential pools are allowed in all Residence Districts. They must meet the accessory-structure setbacks, which also apply to pumps, filters and other pool equipment.
A building permit from the Building Official is required before a pool is built, installed, enlarged or altered.
Plans must show the pool's dimensions and construction, distances to lot lines, buildings, walks and fences, the water supply and drainage, and sections through the pool showing depth.

The pool enclosure, gates included, must be at least five feet high. Gates must be self-latching and lockable, with latches at least four feet above the ground, and the apron between fence and pool edge must be at least four feet wide.

sources.title: Town of Barrington Zoning Ordinance, section 185-15 Swimming pool requirements (eCode360)

jurisdictions.name: Middletown
jurisdictions.office: Town of Middletown Building & Zoning Department
notes: Middletown's Building & Zoning Department says in-ground and above-ground pools need a building permit, and its pool page links to separate electrical and plumbing permit applications.
A 48-inch-high pool barrier is required if the pool can hold 24 inches of water.
The page links to the 2021 Rhode Island Swimming Pool & Spa Code and to the town's permit, inspection and barrier requirements.

sources.title: Residential Pools & Hot Tubs (Town of Middletown)

jurisdictions.name: South Kingstown (Washington County)
jurisdictions.office: Town of South Kingstown Building & Zoning Department
notes: The town's FAQ says a building permit, a site plan and structural detail, along with an electrical permit, are required for any pool that can hold 24 inches or more of water, and all pools must be at least 10 feet from any property line.

The town's pool requirements sheet says the barrier must be at least 48 inches above grade, measured on the side facing away from the pool, and at least 20 inches from the water's edge, and pedestrian gates must open outward away from the pool, be self-closing and have a self-latching device.

The sheet says the building permit does not cover electrical, plumbing or mechanical work, which all need separate permits obtained online. The department's page says all inspections must be called in to the Building Official's office, cannot be scheduled through the Online Permitting System, and at least 24 hours' notice is preferred.

For an in-ground pool, the sheet lists inspections from rebar and rebar bonding, before concrete is poured or gunite is sprayed, through a final inspection for use and occupancy before the pool is used, and says the pool cannot be used until all necessary inspections and safety measures are permanently in place.

sources.title: Requirements - Pools and Hot Tubs (Town of South Kingstown)
Building & Zoning FAQs (Town of South Kingstown)
Building & Zoning Department (Town of South Kingstown)

state_level.note: The Rhode Island Swimming Pool and Spa Code (510-RICR-00-00-14) adopts the 2021 edition of the International Swimming Pool and Spa Code, with state amendments.

source.title: Rhode Island Swimming Pool and Spa Code, 510-RICR-00-00-14 (RI Department of State)
